NextItNet uses residual causal dilated convolutions to expand receptive fields while computing sequence positions in parallel. Its autoregressive objective supports next-item supervision at every valid position: align input prefixes with one-step-shifted targets, exclude padding from loss, and prevent future information leakage. For this task’s left-padded histories, inference must select the final nonpadding position. These changes retain one NextItNet backbone and scoring head per category. [Original NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf).

Implementation inference: compute sequence features once, flatten valid training positions, then score a shared pool of sampled item embeddings using matrix multiplication. Mine negatives from detached scores under the same current model; exclude padding and each row’s positive, then recompute selected logits with gradients for cross-entropy over the positive and selected negatives. Hard-negative research supports model-dependent sampling, but deterministic top-k selection is not an unbiased full-softmax estimator and offers no guaranteed HR improvement. [Hard-negative analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.06245). Chunk feature rows or candidate columns to bound mining memory, maintaining running per-row top-k across candidate chunks. During inference, reuse the final sequence feature across all candidate chunks. Chunking reduces temporary score storage; it does not reduce the total number of dot products. PyTorch’s implementation similarly illustrates chunked linear cross-entropy computation. [PyTorch source](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/nn/modules/linear_cross_entropy.py).
